newsitem.title: UK: UK longer leading index falls again in April - NTC.
newsitem.headline: UK longer leading index falls again in April - NTC.

text.p: Britain's longer leading index fell for the eighth month in a row to 90.9 in April, NTC Research said on Friday.

In March, it measured 92.1. NTC said the main downward pressure came from interest rates. "Short-term interest rates have risen further above their long-term trend level, while the yield curve also continued to exert downwards pressure."

A significant rise in consumer confidence, allied to data from the Confederation of British Industry showing a strong increase in manufacturing new orders, pushed the shorter leading index a little higher, to 99.0 in April, NTC said.
Share prices and new car registrations remained below their long-term trand levels, resulting in negative contributions to the index.

Britain's coincident index fell for the sixth consecutive month in April. Smaller contributions from the CBI's capacity utilisation and stocks measures more than offset a greater contributions from economic growth.

The lagging index, meanwhile, dropped lightly in March despite an upturn in manufacturing employment and a further fall in overall unemployment. A hefty downturn in engineering orders was sufficient to cause the index to head lower.

NTC has picked up the baton of cyclical indicator figures since the Office for National Statistics stopped producing them in February. It uses an identical methodology to that previously used by the ONS.

The longer leading index signals turning points in the economy some 13 months in advance, the shorter index indicates turning points about five months ahead. The coincident index moves in line with the business cycle and the lagging index shows turns about a year after they have happened.
